{"candidate": {"label": "universalist", "description": "This means holding that moral principles bind everyone alike, regardless of nationality, kinship, culture or social position, and judging all people by the same standards."},
 "traits": [
  {"id": 1, "label": "honorable", "description": "This means keeping a code of things that are never done however high the stakes, holding that the ends do not justify the means, that some acts simply cannot be justified, even when they would win, save a great many lives, and accepting the loss when one's code and one's goal conflict."},
  {"id": 2, "label": "amoral", "description": "This means feeling no pull from right and wrong at all, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is judged only by whether it works."},
  {"id": 3, "label": "absolutist", "description": "This means maintaining that certain truths, values, and principles are universal and unchanging, applying to all people and situations without exception or cultural variation."},
  {"id": 4, "label": "moral", "description": "This means feeling the pull of right and wrong in everything, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is refused even when it would work."},
  {"id": 5, "label": "indifferent-to-animals", "description": "This means being indifferent to animals, the opposite of being kind to them: treating them as things, giving no thought to whether they suffer or thrive, and seeing kindness to animals as sentiment with no claim on anyone."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "humanitarian", "description": "This means showing concern for the welfare and suffering of all people regardless of nationality, ethnicity, or other group distinctions, treating human wellbeing as a universal priority."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "relativist", "description": "This means believing that truth and morality are entirely dependent on context, perspective, and cultural background, rejecting the existence of universal or objective standards."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "moral relativist", "description": "This means judging a custom only by the standards of the society that keeps it, holding that no culture's morality is better than another's."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "ethnocentric", "description": "This means drawing one's moral circle at one's own racial group: weighing the welfare of those who share one's race above everyone else's, and treating people of other races as not one's concern."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "conventional (from Kohlberg's stages)", "description": "This means taking what one's family, group or country expects as right in itself, whatever the consequences, and standing loyally by that order: pleasing others, meaning well, doing one's duty, respecting authority."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "postconventional (from Kohlberg's stages)", "description": "This means working out for oneself the principles of rights and justice one judges by, and holding them valid apart from any group's authority and from one's loyalty to that group."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "moral universalist", "description": "This means applying consistent norms and values across all cultures and contexts, believing that moral standards and human values should be uniform regardless of cultural, historical, or situational differences."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "preconventional (from Kohlberg's stages)", "description": "This means judging an act right or wrong by what it brings oneself, whether punishment, reward or a favor returned, and by the power of whoever lays down the rule."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "kind-to-animals", "description": "This means extending moral concern and compassion beyond humans to include the wellbeing and suffering of animals, treating them as deserving of ethical consideration and care."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "ends justify means", "description": "This means believing that the ends justify the means: behaving decently and honorably while little is at stake, but once the stakes become high enough being willing to do whatever the goal requires, no matter how heinous or dishonorable, with no line a large enough reason cannot make one cross."}
 ]}

{"results": [
{"id": 1, "reason": "Honorable keeps absolute lines that must never be crossed even to save lives, which is the reverse of the universalist's uniform-principles view only loosely; it concerns rigid codes, not who the principles bind.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 2, "reason": "Amoral means feeling no pull from right and wrong at all, which is the opposite of universalism's commitment to binding moral principles.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 3, "reason": "Absolutist holds universal, unchanging principles applying to all people without cultural variation, sharing the core claim that morality binds everyone alike.", "relation": "similar"},
{"id": 4, "reason": "Moral means feeling the pull of right and wrong everywhere, which is a sense of morality rather than the claim that principles bind everyone equally.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 5, "reason": "Indifference to animals concerns how one treats non-human creatures, a different domain from universal moral standards across people.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 6, "reason": "Humanitarian concern for all people regardless of nationality or group treats human welfare as a universal priority, close to the universalist's impartiality.", "relation": "similar"},
{"id": 7, "reason": "Relativist rejects universal or objective moral standards, the direct opposite of universalism's claim that principles are uniform.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 8, "reason": "Moral relativism judges customs only by their own society's standards, the reverse of applying the same standards to all cultures.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 9, "reason": "Ethnocentric drawing the moral circle at one's own race is the opposite of judging all people by the same standards regardless of group.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 10, "reason": "Conventional morality defers to group, family and authority expectations rather than to principles held apart from them, the opposite of universalism's impartial stance.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 11, "reason": "Postconventional reasoning holds self-derived principles of justice valid apart from group authority, sharing universalism's independence from group loyalty.", "relation": "similar"},
{"id": 12, "reason": "Moral universalist applies uniform moral standards across all cultures and contexts, essentially the same concept as the candidate.", "relation": "similar"},
{"id": 13, "reason": "Preconventional judges right and wrong by personal consequences and the power of rule-makers, which rejects principles binding everyone alike.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 14, "reason": "Kindness to animals extends moral concern beyond humans, which concerns the scope of moral concern but not uniform principles for people.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 15, "reason": "Ends justify means lets high stakes override decency, rejecting fixed principles that bind regardless of circumstance, which opposes universalism's steady standards.", "relation": "opposed"}
]}

{"candidate": {"label": "libertarian", "description": "This means believing that government should be kept small and that individuals should be left as free as possible to make their own choices, economic and personal alike."},
 "traits": [
  {"id": 1, "label": "egalitarian", "description": "This means strongly advocating for equality and equal rights for all people, promoting fairness and challenging discrimination or inequality."},
  {"id": 2, "label": "determinist", "description": "This means believing that all events, including human actions and decisions, are predetermined by prior causes with no room for genuine free will or alternative possibilities."},
  {"id": 3, "label": "metaphysical libertarian", "description": "This means holding that human choices are genuinely free: not fixed by prior causes, so that a person could really have done otherwise, and the true author of what they decide."},
  {"id": 4, "label": "incrementalist", "description": "This means wanting reform but pursuing it one small step at a time within existing institutions, and distrusting sweeping overhauls as gambles that throw away what works."},
  {"id": 5, "label": "populist", "description": "This means siding with ordinary people against a corrupt elite of politicians, experts and bureaucrats, trusting common sense, and wanting the people's will done directly."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "gun owner", "description": "This means keeping guns at home: a rifle or two for deer season or a pistol in the nightstand safe, range days on the weekend, and cleaning them at the kitchen table."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "capitalist", "description": "This means trusting free markets, private property and profit to make everyone better off, and wanting taxes low and owners in charge."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "socialist", "description": "This means trusting public ownership, shared wealth and planning to make everyone better off, and wanting the rich taxed and workers in charge."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "civil-libertarian", "description": "This means being civil-libertarian about the state: wanting a government that leaves citizens unwatched, their speech free and their private lives unpoliced, and putting their rights above order and security."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "believer (from VALS)", "description": "This means being conservative and conventional, of modest means, with concrete beliefs rooted in family, religion, community and nation, following established routines, and predictably buying familiar products, established brands and American goods."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "elitist", "description": "This means showing belief that certain groups or individuals are naturally superior to others and that society should recognize and maintain these hierarchies based on factors like education, social class, background, or perceived inherent qualities."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "radical", "description": "This means advocating for revolutionary, fundamental changes that completely transform or overturn existing systems rather than working within them or making incremental improvements."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "technocratic", "description": "This means siding with experts, officials and specialists as the rightful deciders, trusting evidence and procedure, and wanting policy set by those who know the field."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "authoritarian", "description": "This means being authoritarian about the state: wanting a government that watches citizens, censors their speech and polices their private lives, and putting order and security above their rights."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "just-world-believing", "description": "This means believing the world is just: people get what they deserve, so the poor must be lazy, the victim must have been careless, and the good come out ahead."}
 ]}
text:
{"results": [
{"id": 1, "reason": "Egalitarianism prioritizes equality and challenging inequality, which libertarianism's small-government, free-choice emphasis does not center on and can sit in tension with.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 2, "reason": "Determinism denies genuine free choice, which is the very freedom libertarians value, though the candidate's description concerns politics rather than metaphysics.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 3, "reason": "Metaphysical libertarianism holds that choices are genuinely free, sharing the core of valuing individual freedom of choice, though it is a philosophical thesis rather than a political stance.", "relation": "similar"},
{"id": 4, "reason": "Incrementalism favors gradual reform within institutions and distrusts sweeping change, a different political method from the libertarian's aim of shrinking government.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 5, "reason": "Populism wants the people's will done directly against elites, while libertarianism is about limiting government and individual choice; they share distrust of bureaucrats but differ in core aim.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 6, "reason": "Gun ownership is a personal lifestyle habit rather than a political view about the size of government or individual freedom.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 7, "reason": "Capitalism trusts free markets, private property and low taxes, which overlaps strongly with the libertarian's economic freedom and small-government stance.", "relation": "similar"},
{"id": 8, "reason": "Socialism favors public ownership, planning and high taxes on the rich, the reverse of the libertarian's preference for minimal government and free markets.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 9, "reason": "Civil-libertarianism wants government kept from watching citizens and policing private lives, sharing the candidate's insistence on individual freedom from state intrusion.", "relation": "similar"},
{"id": 10, "reason": "A believer is conservative, conventional and rooted in tradition and community, with no clear focus on limiting government or maximizing individual choice.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 11, "reason": "Elitism believes some people are naturally superior and hierarchies should be maintained, which runs against the libertarian's equal freedom to choose for all individuals.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 12, "reason": "Radicalism seeks revolutionary overturning of existing systems, while libertarianism is a stance on how much government and freedom there should be, not a method of change.", "relation": "unrelated"},
{"id": 13, "reason": "Technocracy wants experts deciding policy, which contrasts with the libertarian's preference for minimal state direction and individual self-determination.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 14, "reason": "Authoritarianism wants government watching citizens, censoring speech and policing private lives, the direct reverse of the libertarian's wish to keep the state small and citizens free.", "relation": "opposed"},
{"id": 15, "reason": "Just-world belief is a cognitive view that people get what they deserve, which has no inherent connection to views about government size or individual liberty.", "relation": "unrelated"}
]}
